title: A C++ wrapper for a C API
description:
Wrap a C handle API in a modern C++ class.

```
xn::Counter c{10};
c.add(5);          -> 15
copy: not allowed; move: allowed
errors become xn::Error exceptions
destroyed once, automatically
```
hints: `struct Deleter { void operator()(CCounter* c) const { c_destroy(c); } };` is a custom deleter, as in the C++ course's smart pointer lesson: `std::unique_ptr<CCounter, Deleter>` then calls `c_destroy` instead of `delete`. Lesson 3.06 shows the rest of the wrapper's shape.
With a `unique_ptr` member, copy is deleted and move works without writing either.
requirements: `class Counter` holds the C handle in a `std::unique_ptr<CCounter, Deleter>`.
Methods call the C functions and throw `xn::Error` on a non-zero code.
Copying is deleted, moving works, and the handle is destroyed exactly once.
stretch: Add `explicit operator bool` and a `release()` that gives the handle back to C code.
